purpose: The normaliser fixture. burkina_faso_sample.pdf (pages 1-4 of the same issue) is only RESULTATS PROVISOIRES, the awards section; it has no tender notice, no deadline and no financing line for a normaliser to parse. This fixture is the AVIS (tender notices) section of the same real issue, so monitor/normalise/burkina_faso.py can be built against actual notices rather than documentation memory.

source_issue.full_issue_not_refetched_note: The full issue was already on disk from this same session's earlier fetch (scratchpad/q4478.pdf, sha256 verified to match full_issue_sha256 above before use); it was not fetched again for this fixture.

table_of_contents_measured.note: Read directly from the issue's own page-1 table of contents (pdftotext -layout -f 1 -l 1). It names two top-level sections: RESULTATS PROVISOIRES (Ministères... P.3, Régions P.12) and AVIS (Ministères: Fournitures et services courants P.20, Travaux and Prestations intellectuelles listed with no page number printed in the ToU cell itself; Régions: Fournitures et services courants P.23, Travaux P.24, Prestations intellectuelles P.47).

extraction.tool: qpdf 11.x (pdftk not installed on this host; qpdf is also what the existing burkina_faso_sample.pdf fixture used, per burkina_faso.json's truncation_note)
extraction.page_range: 20-47 (1-indexed, inclusive, matching the task's instruction and the table of contents' own AVIS start/last-entry pages)
extraction.text_layer_chars_note: As measured by monitor.normalise.ocr.extract (len(text.strip())), the same call path the connector's own contract test already uses for burkina_faso_sample.pdf; a raw `pdftotext -layout -enc UTF-8 | wc -m` on this file reads 125847 before that trailing-whitespace strip.
extraction.fonts_note: pdffonts on both the full issue and this extraction show the same mixed pattern: several font names (TimesNewRomanPSMT, Arial-BoldMT, ArialMT, Arial-ItalicMT, Arial-BoldItalicMT, TimesNewRomanPS-ItalicMT, TimesNewRomanPS-BoldItalicMT) appear twice, once as a non-embedded WinAnsi TrueType reference (emb=no, standard Word/Windows font names Office does not bother embedding) and once as an embedded, unicode-mapped CID TrueType subset (emb=yes) carrying the actual glyphs used. At least one embedded font is present and pdftotext extracts real prose either way; this is the same pattern the original sample_pdf fixture's issue already showed, not a regression introduced by qpdf's page extraction.
extraction.boundary_check_page_19: Still RESULTATS PROVISOIRES at page 19 (a synthese des resultats for REGION DE YAADGA) -- confirms page 20 is the true start of AVIS, not one page early.
extraction.boundary_check_page_47: Last page of the extraction ends mid-notice: an Avis de Manifestation d'Interet for COMMUNE DE TENKODOGO (suivi-controle de travaux, auberge communale) whose clauses 1-2 and lot list appear on page 47 but whose clauses 3-6, signature and deadline (15/09/2026) continue on page 48, one page outside this fixture's declared range -- see truncation_note below.
extraction.truncation_note: The task specified pages 20-47 (matching the table of contents' own last-listed AVIS entry, 'Marches de prestations intellectuelles ... P. 47' under Regions), and this fixture follows that instruction exactly. Measured independently of that instruction: the issue's actual AVIS content does not end cleanly at the foot of page 47 -- the final notice (Commune de Tenkodogo, Avis de Manifestation d'Interet) continues onto page 48 with its submission deadline, address and signature block, and page 49 is a closing masthead/footer page with no notice content. A normaliser built only against this fixture will see one notice (the last one) truncated before its deadline field; this is recorded here rather than silently worked around, per this session's own instruction not to build a second selector or a fallback path. Whoever builds the normaliser should decide, with a person, whether the connector's real per-issue extraction (not this fixture) needs to run a page or two past a printed 'P. NN' table-of-contents entry to reach an actual section boundary, since this issue shows the two are not always the same page.

measured_inventory.method: re.findall(pattern, text, re.IGNORECASE) against monitor.normalise.ocr.extract(fixture).text -- the exact text the normaliser itself will receive -- rather than a shell pdftotext invocation, so these counts are not sensitive to a locale mismatch (the host's default POSIX locale silently drops matches on accented characters under `grep -i` and undercounted every accented marker by roughly half when first tried with LC_ALL unset; recomputed with LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 first, then cross-checked against ocr.extract's own text, which matches).
measured_inventory.avis_de_demande_de_prix_note: Case-insensitive count of the literal phrase, including its 11 occurrences inside 'Cet Avis de demande de prix fait suite à...' recital prose as well as the marker line itself; this is a phrase count, not a distinct-notice count, and the normaliser needs its own rule (most likely: only the marker line immediately under a title line, not every recital sentence) to turn this into a notice count.
measured_inventory.avis_d_appel_d_offres_note: Matched both straight (') and curly (’) apostrophes in 'appel d'offres' / 'd'offres'; both forms occur in this fixture.
measured_inventory.manifestation_d_interet_note: Matched both apostrophe forms and both 'intérêt'/'interet' accent renderings; all 4 use the accented curly-apostrophe form 'manifestation d’intérêt' in this fixture.
measured_inventory.depot_des_offres_note: Matched 'dépôt des offres' and 'depot des offres' spelling variants; every occurrence in this fixture uses the fully accented form.
measured_inventory.montant_previsionnel_note: Includes both the standalone header line ('Montant prévisionnel : ...') and the recital sentence ('Le montant prévisionnel de la présente demande de prix est ...') that restates the same figure later in most notices -- these are typically a pair per notice, not two distinct amounts. Two notices print the header phrase twice in a row on the same line ('Montant prévisionnel : Montant prévisionnel HTVA et TTC : ...'), which is why this is 47 rather than 2x the 22-23 notices actually carrying a figure; counted as instances of the phrase, not as lines, since a line-based count silently drops that duplication.

montant_previsionnel_sample_lines_note: Ten real *physical* lines exactly as `pdftotext -layout` emits them (poppler wraps a long sentence at the page's print width, so several of these end mid-clause or mid-word rather than at a full stop -- that break point is real and reproducible, not an editing artefact, and quoting the wrapped line rather than a hand-joined sentence is what makes these safe to assert against verbatim). Chosen to show the format variety a normaliser's XOF parser has to handle: bare digits with space-separated thousands ('9 322 034'), digits with a semicolon separating HTVA and TTC figures, fully spelled-out French number words with the digit figure repeated in parentheses, and three different currency-unit spellings for the same currency -- 'FCFA', 'francs cfa' / 'francs CFA' (lower and upper case c), and 'F CFA' (space before CFA) -- plus 'HTVA' (hors taxe sur la valeur ajoutee) and 'TTC' (toutes taxes comprises), and one notice ('trente-trois millions...') that prints the 'Montant prévisionnel' header phrase twice in a row on the same line.
buyer_heading_lines_verbatim: INSTITUT SUPERIEUR DE LOGISTIQUE DE OUAGADOUGOU
INSTITUT NATIONAL DE FORMATION DES PERSONNEL DE L’EDUCATION
buyer_heading_lines_note: The nearest all-caps line above each of the first three 'Avis de demande de prix' marker lines in reading order (each is two text lines above the marker: buyer name, then a one-line notice title, then the marker itself -- not directly adjacent). Verbatim as pdftotext -layout extracted them: accented capitals are printed unaccented ('SUPERIEUR', not 'SUPÉRIEUR'; confirmed byte-for-byte with od -c, no missing-glyph substitution, this is simply how the source PDF renders uppercase accents), while a lowercase apostrophe-linked word keeps its curly apostrophe and lowercase accent ('L’EDUCATION' -- capital E, no accent, same unaccented-capital pattern). A buyer-name heuristic keyed on 'this line is capitals' must not also require accented capitals to match, or it will miss buyers with accented names.
